prerequisites: Mechanical and metallurgical concepts of mechanical behavior

learning_outcomes.text: Be acquainted with steel microstructures and cast iron, and relate them with chemical composition and cooling velocities on the various heat treatments
Be able to relate microstructures with mechanic properties: resistance, ductility and tenacity
Be acquainted with the nomenclature and objectives of the metal alloys and thermal treatments
Be able to discuss steel, cast iron and non-ferrous alloys selection based on the mechanical properties depending on the function of chemical composition
Be able to understand thermal treatments for pre-defined objectives

Be able to foresee the need of material, coatings, superficial chemical and thermo chemical treatments selection, taking into account the resistance to corrosion, unproblematic production and recyclability

syllabus_topics: Manufacturing process of steel and cast iron
Types of steels: construction, tools, stainless and structural precipitation
Cast iron: gray, ductile, white, malleable and treated
Copper and its alloys: brass and bronze
Material selection software: the CES Edupack
teaching_methods: Study visit to a steel company

assessment_methods.method: Laboratory work (class participation, homeworks, practical assessment, and practical work)

assessment_rules: The final grade (CF) is calculated as 30% of the practical part (CP) grade plus 70% of the final or second exam (CE) grade: CF = 0.3 * CP + 0.7 * CE. To pass, a minimum grade of 7.00 points (out of 20) is required in both the CE and CP components. The grade in the CP component cannot be 6 points higher than the grade in the CE component. Only the exam part (CE) can be improved, using the same formula for calculation, and presence in at least 75% of laboratory classes is mandatory for final exam admission.
